title: Nested Loops & Loop‑Else 🧠
description: Combine loops for multi‑dimensional tasks and use the `else` clause to detect when a loop completes normally.

slides.title: Loop Within a Loop
slides.content:
# For Multi‑Host, Multi‑Port Scanning

When you need to scan every port on every host, you nest a `for` loop inside another:
```python
hosts = ["10.0.0.1", "10.0.0.2"]
ports = [22, 80]
for host in hosts:
    for port in ports:
        print(f"Scanning {host}:{port}")
```
Output:
```
Scanning 10.0.0.1:22
Scanning 10.0.0.1:80
Scanning 10.0.0.2:22
Scanning 10.0.0.2:80
```

slides.title: Mixing while and for Nesting
slides.content:
# Any Loop Can Contain Any Other

```python
while not queue.empty():
    item = queue.get()
    for listener in listeners:
        listener.send(item)
```
Perfect for real‑time packet processing.

slides.title: Deep Nesting Alert ⚠️
slides.content:
## 3+ Levels Hurts Readability

If you're nesting three deep, consider breaking inner loops into functions. Your brain will thank you later.

quizData.question: When does the `else` block of a `for` loop execute?

options.text: Only if the loop was not exited by a `break`
Only if the loop body never executed

quizData.explanation: The else clause runs on normal completion (no break).

slides.title: Loop‑else with while
slides.content:
# Works the Same

```python
attempts = 3
while attempts > 0:
    if try_login():
        print("Logged in")
        break
    attempts -= 1
else:
    print("Account locked")
```
If login succeeds, break skips the else. If all attempts fail, else runs.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## The name `else` is confusing

Some think it should have been called `nobreak`. Just remember: `else` means "no break".
